# 1.19.4

The settings update: all 231 settings you picked (new MORE pages, a SEARCH tab, page numbers), plus everything else from the testing builds since 1.19.3: the new map pool with a legacy maps toggle, ball mode, winner stays and power modes, the dash slide, no air drift, rocket knockback doubled, walk teleporters, one race leaderboard over every race map, and the fullscreen size warning. **The network protocol is now 66 (1.19.3 used 53): 1.19.4 doesn't play with 1.19.3 games or servers**, so update both. Dedicated servers update themselves. Maps saved by 1.19.4 are format 13: 1.19.3 can't open them; older maps convert by themselves. Your settings, maps, demos and files are kept. Human-made assets: 16.1%.

## Settings (the settings update, batch 1 of the 231 you picked)
- **New MORE pages** on CONTROLS and VIDEO + AUDIO (button at the bottom middle) for settings that didn't fit.
- **Mouse:** vertical sensitivity, invert Y, zoom sensitivity (x1.00 = the same feel as unzoomed).
- **Scoreboard:** hold or toggle.
- **Window:** window size picker, the window's size and position kept between launches, and a 10 second "keep these display settings?" that puts the old mode back if you don't click KEEP.
- **Background:** an FPS cap while alt-tabbed or minimized (60 by default) and an optional mute.
- **Shadow quality** low / medium / high, applied at once. The GPU's name is shown, and laptops with two GPUs now run the game on the dedicated one.
- **HUD size:** every HUD element bigger or smaller at once.
- **Crosshair:** dot size, opacity, outline thickness and opacity, a style per weapon (e.g. a dot on the sniper), and COPY / PASTE CODE to share a crosshair in one line.
- **Hitsounds:** their own volume, any sound pack's hitsound, a headshot ding, and the kill sound on its own switch.
- **Server list:** sort by ping / players / name, hide full / empty, a ping limit, favourites (right-click a server; listed first) and a RECENT button for the servers you joined last.
- **Race and surf:** tap R to go back to your last checkpoint, or hold it a quarter of a second to restart from the start. FULL RESTART can also go on a key of its own (CONTROLS > MORE KEYS). Both can be rebound.

## Settings (batch 2, first half)
- **More MORE pages:** GAMEPLAY gets one, and VIDEO + AUDIO now has three. CONTROLS has a third keys page, MORE KEYS.
- **Picture:** gamma, contrast and saturation for the 3D scene (the HUD stays as it is), fog amount or off, and render scale now goes from 25% to 400%.
- **Presets:** LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / COMPETITIVE set shadows, anti-aliasing, render scale, fog and effects in one go.
- **Effects:** effects opacity (explosions, sparks, bursts; 0 = off), kill bursts, tracers and the gun's recoil kick on their own switches.
- **Colour blindness:** two team colour presets for red-green and blue-yellow colour blindness, and a warning under the team colours when your pair would be hard to tell apart.
- **Enemy model:** draw every enemy as one model (not in ranked).
- **Sound:** separate volumes for your footsteps, other players' footsteps (up to 2x louder), gunfire and the bomb beep. **The planted bomb now beeps**, faster as it runs down.
- **Kill feed and chat:** how long lines stay, how many show, only kills you're in, chat opacity. While typing, the mouse wheel or Page Up / Down scrolls back through chat.
- **Team chat:** a TEAM CHAT key sends to your team only (shown as "(TEAM)").
- **More keys:** LAST WEAPON, SPEC NEXT / SPEC PREV while dead or spectating, HIDE HUD (with an option to keep the crosshair). When a new bind takes a key from another action, the page says so, with an UNDO button.
- **HUD:** FPS and ping in the top right without a widget, announcer captions, health bars that fill to the mode's max health instead of 100, and a headshot colour for the crosshair's hit flash. Hints that name a key (like "HOLD E" to plant) now show your own bind.
- **Controls:** grapple hold or toggle, left-handed (gun on the left, grapple launcher on the right), and NEXT / PREV WEAPON can stop at the ends and skip weapons you pick.
- **Display:** G-SYNC / FreeSync mode (vsync on with the frame cap 3 under the refresh), and fullscreen can stay on screen when you alt-tab.
- **Windows:** CPU priority HIGH as an option (above normal stays the default).
- **Menus:** settings can open on the last tab you used, QUIT / DISCONNECT / STOP HOSTING can ask "SURE?" first, and a RECONNECT button on the main menu joins your last server again.
- **Connection:** if the connection drops, the game tries to reconnect by itself (3 times; it can be turned off).
- **Queues:** when your queue fills, a chime plays and the taskbar button flashes if the game is in the background.
- **Map editor:** redo (Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z), and an autosave every minute while you have unsaved changes, with RESTORE AUTOSAVE if the game closed before you saved.

## Settings (batch 2, second half)
- **Settings search:** a SEARCH box at the top of settings. Type part of a setting's name (or a key's) and click a match to jump to its page.
- **Three keys per action:** every action can now have three keys instead of two.
- **Console binds:** `bind`, `unbind`, `binds`, `alias`, `unalias`, `exec` and `toggle` in the console. A key can run any console command, and `autoexec.cfg` in the data folder runs at start.
- **Export / import all settings:** GAMEPLAY > MORE > ALL SETTINGS copies every setting to the clipboard, or reads them back; RESET ALL (click twice) goes back to the defaults, keeping your name and servers.
- **Demos:** sort by date, name, size or map, each demo's size, DELETE, AUTO RECORD (every match or ranked only) and KEEP the newest N.
- **Sensitivity from another game:** CONTROLS > MORE turns a CS2, Quake, Apex, TF2, Valorant, Overwatch or Call of Duty sensitivity into Quark's.
- **Fullscreen resolution:** VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 3 picks any mode your monitor offers.
- **Practice (your own server, alone with bots):** pause > PRACTICE has save / load position, god mode, passive bots (they don't shoot) and reset.
- **Players:** pause > PLAYERS lists everyone on your server, with KICK, ADD BOT, KICK BOTS and RESTART.
- **Race ghost:** in race and surf, your best run on each map plays as a see-through ghost.
- **Team panel and match summary:** an optional panel with your teammates' health, and a summary of your match (shots, hits, accuracy, damage, best streak) under the end-of-match scoreboard.

## Settings (batch 3: video, audio, crosshair, network, accessibility)
- **More picture options:** VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 2 adds TONE CURVE, CLEAN SURFACES, FLAT LIGHTING, SIMPLE SKY, FAR SCENERY, DRAW DISTANCE (150 / 250 / 400 m), DEBAND and 10-BIT OUTPUT, plus tracer colour (classic, team or your own) and projectile TRAILS (off / short / full, with opacity).
- **MSAA 8x**, and options your PC can't do now say "N/A" (MSAA levels, 10-bit, latent sync, bypass compositor).
- **New VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 4:** shadow edge, shadow distance, shadows on the map / on players, your own shadow, players always lit, player brightness, custom outline colours and opacity, separate team / enemy outline widths, rope colour, fixed team A / B colours when spectating or watching demos, colour scheme copy / paste and 3 save slots, and accessibility: REDUCE FLASHING, colourblind-safe OK / error colours, tag "it" and race splits in your palette, AHEAD / BEHIND on splits.
- **New VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 5 (sound):** mono / swapped channels, stereo width, behind-you muffle, hearing range, sound occlusion (walls muffle sounds), dynamic range (clean / normal / night), audio latency (low / normal / safe), volume in dB or on a perceptual curve and up to 150%, background volume, force your sound pack on everyone, streak callouts (all / mine / off), time warnings (off / 60 + 30 / countdown, and on screen), each cue sound and announcer line on or off, and VISUALIZE SOUNDS.
- **New VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 6:** a NET GRAPH (apart from F3), packet loss protection 2 / 4 / 8, map downloads on / off with a cache limit and CLEAR, the light bake cache (size, bake threads, CLEAR), FOV as horizontal / vertical / 4:3, bypass compositor (Linux), latent sync safety and late-frame behaviour (Windows), a bigger or coloured menu cursor, and USE as hold or toggle.
- **Crosshair:** a spread circle, a cooldown ring, and sizes in exact pixels instead of scaled with the resolution.

## Settings (batch 3: HUD, social, controls, menus, host, editor, launcher)
- **Hit feedback (GAMEPLAY > MORE 2):** damage number colour, stacking and time; damage direction arcs (colour, size, time); kill mark time and colour; a KILLED <NAME> line; hit flash time; low health warning (threshold, colour, pulse, beep); green +N heal numbers; weapon kick amount; and per weapon: show its model, and move it (x, y, depth).
- **HUD info (GAMEPLAY > MORE 3):** speed in m/s, km/h or ups with a scale and ticks; bar captions; a 12 h clock, the round clock counting up and tenths in the last 10 s; pick the verbose info lines; auto-hide health, weapon list and bars; objective marker size, opacity, distance and edge arrow; scope size and reticle colour / width; network warnings (ping, loss, stall); a minimal spectator HUD; a headshot mark in the kill feed; a stalemate warning before the drain.
- **Social (GAMEPLAY > MORE 4):** team chat only, a word filter, one chat colour, timestamps, your name highlighted with a ping, system messages all / important / off, a chat box with its own opacity, scoreboard sort and columns, others' name colours on or off, streamer mode (hides addresses, codes and names), alerts when the game is in the background, and what to do on joining (play, spectate, ask). Death camera: on the killer, your body or a teammate, for 0 to 3 s; spectator FOV and third person.
- **Controls (CONTROLS > MORE 2):** per-weapon sensitivity, alt-fire toggle and swapped fire buttons; mouse acceleration and raw input; auto-hop off; a console key of your choice and the console in menus; alt-fire toggles allowed in ranked. New binds: volume up / down / mute, record demo, join team, spectate. Mode profiles can now set sensitivity, FOV and zoom FOV.
- **Menus (PLAYER > MORE):** menu theme (dark or high contrast), your own accent, text brightness, panel darkness; the menu background as clockwork, a map you pick or a plain colour; the data folder with OPEN; your quip; mods (use your overrides, open the folders); remember your ranked queues; hide ratings. PLAYER shows your model turning in your colours (drag to turn it).
- **HUD:** the objective line, the notices and the scoreboard can now be moved, sized, coloured or hidden on the HUD tab like the other elements. Custom widgets get 8 more values (snapshot rate, accuracy, damage, streak, round, vertical speed, height, weapon).
- **Players and votes:** pause > PLAYERS is open to everyone: block one player's quips. New votes: restart, 5 more minutes, shuffle teams, kick a player.
- **Hosting:** tick rate, snapshot rate and upload cap; auto start; balance bot skill; vs bots up to 15 a side.
- **Editor:** fly keys follow your binds, fast-fly multiplier, a custom grid, a rotation step, the fly speed, grid and last light are remembered; test play picks the mode, bots, starts at the camera and can skip warmup.
- **Race:** splits against your best, the previous segment or your last run, with a display time; the race stats page picks the map and the date format.
- **Launcher:** OPTIONS: start the game automatically, keep the launcher open, launch options, and updates automatic / ask / at next launch.

## Settings (batch 4: colours, screenshots, sound extras, latency)
- **New VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 7 (colours):** the world's outline colour, a wallbang tint, a high-contrast map palette, your own sky and glow colours on every map, objectives in your palette, zone pulse and opacity, a colour per FFA opponent, your own colour for your shots / laser / rope, gun colour (map / team / custom), health bar low threshold and colours, name tag colour / opacity / size, explosion colours (their own / your team / custom) and a colourblind palette for F3.
- **New VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 8:** screenshots as PNG or TGA, saved in the game's folder or Pictures/Quark, with or without the HUD, and an OPEN FOLDER button; demo rate (also here, not only on DEMOS); always on top; dash buffer (off / 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.15 s); ultra low-latency safety margin; NVIDIA threaded optimization off and DXGI present (Windows); hitsound tiers on / off, typing sounds on / off, quip captions and announcer ducking.
- **MORE 2:** liquids flowing or still, glow strength, SMOOTH strength and the lightmap filter (smooth / nearest).

## Settings (batch 4: HUD, menus, social, editor, practice)
- **New HUD > MORE:** your own colours for recharging bars, the speed meter (slow to fast), weapons you can't use, the sticky counter at its most, warning and info lines, and headshot / big-hit damage numbers; the text outline's width (none to thick); how many notices show and for how long; a compass and a radar (teammates and objectives only, not in ranked); hide the REC indicator; tourney's TAB shows the bracket or the scoreboard.
- **Gameplay:** STAIR SMOOTHING off steps the view up stairs at once (GAMEPLAY > MORE 3). SHOW I'M TYPING off hides your "..." from others, and the tiebreak's rock-paper-scissors cards can be clicked (GAMEPLAY > MORE 4).
- **Menus and bots (PLAYER > MORE):** FIXED LOGO COLORS keeps the title cyan / red; your server's bots can all wear the standard model, and take names from `bots/names.txt`.
- **Editor:** CLIP BOX COLOR (CONTROLS > MORE 2). **Race:** SPLITS: PALETTE also colours your best run and the leaderboard's #1.

## Movement fixes
- Wall teleporters keep your speed. Going in fast used to throw you out at a crawl about half the time (surfy too).
- **Walk teleporters:** a teleporter can now let you out at walking speed instead of carrying all your speed (map editor: SPEED: CARRY / WALK on a teleporter; the one you go into decides). **Maps are now format 12**: older maps convert by themselves, but an older game can't open a map with a walk teleporter.
- The grapple can't hook clip any more: it hits it and lets go, like nograpple. No more invisible hook points on map lids.

## Maps
- **Thin walls are shoot-through:** any surface 1/8 m thick or less (coats, panels, thin trim) now lets hitscan through at wallbang damage, like the dark grey wallbang walls.
- **Map picker:** lists only the maps made for the mode you picked (ranked: only that ladder's maps), 7 across, each with a picture of the map from above. The mouse wheel scrolls when there are more.
- **Two new maps, made by q:** **Surfy** (surf), now the map surf mode starts on, and **Cobblestone**.

## Servers
- **Testing server alone:** `install.sh --testing-only` sets up just the testing server, on the normal port, and keeps it running all the time on the newest testing build or production release, whichever is newer. Both servers stay the default (`--both` to go back); `--no-testing` is still production only.
- **OFFICIAL tag:** the official Quark servers (production and testing) show a gold OFFICIAL tag in the server list and are listed first. It goes by the server's address, so another server can't get it by putting "official" in its name.

## Modes
- **New mode: POWER.** Each team shares one health pool, 2500 for every player on it, and nobody dies. An enemy's hits come off your team's pool instead of your health. When a team's pool runs out it loses; when the 10 minutes are up, the fuller pool wins. Your own rockets and the world (lava, acid, falls) take nothing from the pool; falling out of the map still respawns you. Someone who joins mid-match adds their 2500. The score box shows both pools, and the bar under it shows yours. Played on Bastion, Orbital and Lodestone. **The network protocol is now 54**, so games and servers update together.

- **Neutral payload's round clock** is now 2 minutes for every player on the teams, counted when the round starts: 4 minutes in a 1v1, 16 in a 4v4 (it was 5 minutes whatever the size).

## Weapons
- **Rockets speed up.** The rocket launcher's rocket now gains 4 m/s every second it flies, on top of its 48 m/s launch speed (52 m/s after a second, 68 m/s at the end of its 5 s life), and keeps speeding up after a rubber bounce. The lob (alt-fire) is unchanged. Bots lead for it, and rocket riding pulls you along at its new speed. **The network protocol is now 55**, so games and servers update together; older demos still play.
- **Rockets speed up much faster.** The rocket still leaves the launcher at 48 m/s but now gains 16 m/s every second: 64 m/s after one second, 80 m/s after two, 128 m/s at the end of its 5 s life (about 440 m). The lob (alt-fire) is unchanged at 33.6 m/s. **The network protocol is now 58**, so games and servers update together; older demos still play.

## Map checks
- **The walk check sees ramps.** The map tests' "can players get from every spawn to every objective" check now walks up wedges, corners and cut slopes up to 45 degrees (the steepest you can walk). Before, every slope counted as a solid block, so routes up a ramp (Mine's haul road and lava ramp, QK7's helix ramps) were reported missing or found only the long way round.

## Bots
- **Bomb bots use every site.** The attackers went for the first bomb site every round, so a site further away (Datacenter's B) never saw them. They now take the sites in turn, round by round. The defenders still guard one site each.

## Map format 11: spawns for one mode
- **A map can give a mode its own spawns**, e.g. a koth hill in a bomb map: `spawn koth-a` / `spawn koth-b` spawns are used only in king of the hill (and koth starts on them when the map has them), never in other modes. Any mode but race and multi point can have a set (`ffa-any`, `bomb-a`, ...). The map editor sets it on a spawn (MODE SET; a white cap marks one). **Maps are now format 11**: older maps convert by themselves, but an older game can't open a map that uses the new spawns.

## Settings: page numbers
- **Every settings tab with more than one page shows its page numbers at the bottom**, with < and > at the ends: click a number to go straight to that page, or the arrows (or the Left / Right arrow keys) for the previous / next page. The arrows stop at the first and last page. The MORE buttons are gone; BACK now leaves settings from any page (Esc still goes back to the tab's first page).
- **Fixed: settings rows drawn over the bottom buttons.** On Windows, VIDEO + AUDIO's MAP COLOR and RESET MAP COLOR sat on top of BACK and MORE. Pages that were too full have moved rows instead: FLAT MAP (FULLBRIGHT, MAP COLOR) is now on VIDEO + AUDIO page 2, EXCLUSIVE AUDIO (Windows) on page 6 under OUTPUT, and SMOOTHING (INTERP) from GAMEPLAY to VIDEO + AUDIO page 7 under NETWORK. SEARCH finds them all.

## Settings: SEARCH tab
- **SEARCH is a settings tab of its own** (the last one): every setting in the game in one list, three wide, scrolled with the mouse wheel or the scrollbar, each with a small tag saying which tab and page it lives on. Type in the field at the top and the list narrows to the settings whose name, values, hint or a few extra keywords have every word you typed: "screen" finds the display mode, fullscreen size, window size, render scale and your monitors; "fov" the field of view and the zoom FOVs. The settings work right there in the list. **Ctrl+F** (or **/**) opens it from any tab; **Esc** clears what you typed. It replaces the small search box at the top right.

## Bots
- **Team order no longer matters:** every bot now decides what to do on the same picture of the world each tick, and who moves first rotates every tick, so it doesn't matter which team or player joined first. At round start, both teams' spawns are picked without either team dodging the other's fresh spawns.

## Bomb
- **Spawns go by role:** the attackers always start at the map's attack spawns and the defenders at the defence spawns, so at halftime the teams swap ends as well as roles. Before, each team kept its own end, so a map built with the attack 1 s closer to a site than the defence gave the same team the short way all match.

## Glass
- **Sloped glass draws as its slope:** glass on a wedge, corner or cut box used to draw as its whole box (a glass dome looked like four slabs floating over the roof). It now draws, and breaks into shards, as its real shape. The same goes for see-through looks and breakable blocks on a slope.

## Race leaderboard: one total over every race map
- **The race board is now a total:** your best time trial on every race and surf map (Particle Accelerator, Jungle Ruins, Rooftop Run, Surfy) added up, fastest first. A map you haven't run counts at its default time, so playing every map pays. Each map's own board is still there.
- **Surf maps have time trials too**, played with surf's rules; their runs go to the boards like race runs.
- **LEADERBOARD:** the RACE TOTAL column, your total and your time on each map under it, and TRIAL MAP to pick which map PLAY TIME TRIAL starts. MY RACE STATS shows what each map adds to your total.
- Viaduct is no longer a ranked race map.

## Maps: the new pool, and legacy maps
- **The old maps are retired.** Temple, Bastion, Hamlet, Lodestone, Viaduct and the rest of the pool before 1.19.6 are gone from the map lists; the new maps (and q's Surfy and Cobblestone) replace them. The menu background is now Castle, and hosting starts on Sewer.
- **LEGACY MAPS** (settings > GAMEPLAY > MAPS, off by default): turn it on to list the old maps again, marked (legacy). They're never ranked. A server or demo that asks for one by name still loads it.
- **Your maps folder is tidied once:** untouched copies of the old official maps that older versions left in your maps folder (they hid the shipped map of that name) move to `maps\legacy\`. Your own and edited maps and downloaded maps aren't touched.
- **Ranked:** qk1-qk8 are ranked on all three ladders. Each ladder starts on the map it's designed for: vanilla 1v1 on Greenhouse, laser vampire on Dojo, instagib on Spire. A ranked server still set to an old ranked map (e.g. `--map temple`) starts on its ladder's map instead.

## Hide and seek
- **The hiders' head start is 5 seconds** (was 30).

## Race and surf
- **No time limit:** a round runs until someone finishes, and the HUD counts your run time up.
## Rockets
- **Rocket splash damage works online again:** since 1.19.3 only a direct rocket hit did damage on a server; a rocket landing on the floor or a wall next to someone did nothing and showed no hit marker. Splash now hurts as it did before.
- **Map votes:** the old (legacy) maps can't be voted unless the server turns them on.
- **Servers:** a new server starts as unranked laser vampire 1v1 on Dojo.
- **Solar System** (surf): 15 stages, Sun to Pluto, each one built from q's own design. It's on the ranked race total (10 min until you've run it).
- **Weapon switch:** holding the scope (right click) while switching from the rifle to the laser no longer stops the laser shooting until you let go.
- **Syringe:** heals half as much: 5 HP a use (was 10), and a throw gives a teammate 15 HP (was 30).
- **Clean surfaces** now cleans every surface, not just the default ones: each custom surface shows as its own average colour, flat, and every face is one colour (no streaks, stripes or darkening near the floor; liquids too).
- **Your maps folder:** the maps update's one-time cleanup no longer moves your own copies of generated maps into legacy/. It only moves old copies of the official maps.
- **Map editor:** clicking a cut box, wedge, corner or tetra selects it where its faces are, not anywhere in its bounding box.
- **Step-up on cut boxes:** a low cut box with an upright side at an angle is stepped onto like a normal box. A steep sloped face still blocks.
- **Floating faces:** surfaces that drew detached from their objects sit on them again: Monorail's deck top floated about 70 cm above the deck, and a staircase flush with a thin wall or rail showed its outline on the wall's far side (Dam). It happened on most maps.
- **Pattern fade** (VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE 2, LOOK): far away or at a grazing angle, a patterned surface fades smoothly to its average colour instead of shimmering, the way lava already did. On by default at lava's distance; FADE DISTANCE moves where it starts (0.25x to 4x) and FADE LENGTH how gradually it fades. Fully faded surfaces skip their pattern, so they draw a little faster too.
- **Alt-tabbed:** the game stops drawing frames while it's in the background or minimized, and everything else keeps running: your connection, the match and a server you're hosting. DRAW IN BACKGROUND (VIDEO + AUDIO > MORE, WHEN UNFOCUSED) turns drawing back on at the background FPS limit.
- **1v1 winner stays** (ranked too): spectators wait in line in the order they joined. When a match ends, the loser goes to the back of the line and the first in line plays the winner. A draw keeps both players. Joining a full 1v1 puts you in line; TEAM SPEC takes you out of it. If a player leaves, the first in line takes the seat.
- **New mode: WINNER STAYS.** 1v1 rounds while everyone else waits in line. Each round's winner stays; the loser goes to the back of the line and the next in line plays the winner. Every round you win counts, and the first to 10 wins the match. It uses the 1v1 rulesets and is offered on every 1v1 map. Unranked.
- **Tourney on any 1v1 map:** every map that offers 1v1 now offers tourney too (it was only some of them).
- **No sound burst after alt-tabbing:** coming back to the game no longer plays a pile of sounds at once. Sounds that waited too long are dropped, and at most 32 new sounds start at once.
- **Accuracy:** the scoreboard's ACC and the match summary are the average of each weapon's own accuracy, so a second of the laser (100 shots) no longer outweighs every other weapon. It starts from 0 each match.
- **Health bars in ranked:** enemy health bars now show in ranked too, when you have them on (they are on by default).
- **Planting and defusing keep knockback:** you still can't move or shoot while planting or defusing, but rockets and blasts push you now (it froze you in place). Knocked out of range, the plant or defuse stops.
- **New VOTE page:** pause > VOTE > MAP / MODE / MODIFIERS. Turn on what the vote should change (GAMEMODE, MODIFIERS, MAP), then pick each in order: the gamemode (OBJECTIVE BASED or PLAYER BASED first, then the mode and its ruleset), the modifiers (damage, speed, gravity, jump, knockback, health, vampire, regen, instagib, self damage, dash, grapple), then the map. One vote changes all of it. Voted modifiers stay through later map and mode votes until a vote sets them back to STANDARD. Not on ranked or time trial servers, or servers running a custom mode.
- **New mode: BALL.** Two teams, a ball in the middle and a goal at each end. Shoot it, blast it or run into it to move it; it slides like a player on ice, at half gravity. Get it into the enemy goal to score; it goes back to the middle. Most goals after 10 minutes wins. Plays on QK8 Canyon (the goals are the end rooms' doors) and Suspension Bridge (across the deck at each tower), and it's in the vote's OBJECTIVE list.
- **Suspension Bridge:** the smoke banks and haze are gone; spilled shipping containers stand where the smoke banks were, so the spawns still can't see each other.
- **No air drift:** holding a direction in the air below run speed no longer speeds you up (it pushed 8 m/s² up to run speed); air strafing is unchanged.
- **Dash slide:** dash down into the floor without holding jump and you slide like on ice until you're back to run speed or press jump. Holding jump still gives the super dash.
- **Ball:** it bounces off everything like rubber. After a goal (or falling out) it waits 3 s before coming back. Rockets, bolts, stickies and thrown knives hit it. A ball moving over 20 m/s into you hurts and knocks you back. The knife pops it up instead of pushing it away, and the laser pushes it 3x harder, while its pull beam now pulls it.
- **Ball:** your grapple catches the ball. It reels the ball in toward you while it pulls you toward the ball.
- **Rocket:** double knockback everywhere: rocket jumps, enemies, the lob and the ball.
- **Ball:** a knife swing pushes the ball once, not every tick of the swing.
- **Ball:** a hit does 1 damage per m/s of the ball's speed relative to you (a 30 m/s hit is 30), still only above 20 m/s.
- **Ball:** it rolls up any ramp, even past 45°, keeping its speed, and launches off the top.
- **Website:** the game's website moves to its own address, https://quark.casa (the old floration.github.io/quark address forwards there).
- **Fullscreen size** now has a warning: don't touch it unless you know what you're doing.

# 1.19.3

Everything from the testing builds since 1.19.1 (1.19.2 was never released on its own, so its changes ship here): new map pieces (wedges, corners, tetras and cut boxes at any angle), 472 map materials (ice, rubber, glass you can shatter, brick walls you can blow open, and 433 new looks: brick, concrete, tile, stone, nature, buildings, industrial, sci-fi and wasteland), plain and breakable versions of brick, cobblestone and glass, a new surf mode with its map Cascade, damage from your own screen (hits count where you saw them), PRIORITIZE GAME on Windows, and the map editor's material picker, FIX MAP and FIX GAPS. **The network protocol is now 53 (1.19.1 used 47): 1.19.3 doesn't play with 1.19.1 games or servers**, so update both. Dedicated servers update themselves. Maps saved by 1.19.3 are format 10: 1.19.1 can't open them; older maps convert by themselves. Your settings, maps, demos and files are kept. Human-made assets: 16.1%.

## Performance
- **New Settings > VIDEO > PRIORITIZE GAME (Windows, on by default)**: while the game has focus, Windows runs its GPU work before other programs' (a YouTube tab, Discord or other hardware-accelerated apps) and gives it a higher CPU priority. Before, a video playing in the background could take a big share of every frame. Alt-tab and the other programs get their normal share back.

- **Blown-open brick and cobblestone walls no longer cut your FPS**: after holes were blown in a wall (or the whole wall fell), every brick and cobblestone pixel on screen kept checking every hole on the map, so a room of brick could drop to a tenth of the frame rate. Each pixel now checks only the holes near it.

## Maps
- **Wedges and corners**: two new map pieces besides boxes. A wedge is a ramp (one top edge kept), a corner a pyramid with one top corner kept; the slope is whatever the box gives, so any angle. They can stand on the floor, hang upside down from a ceiling or lie on their side (an angled wall). Slopes up to 45 degrees are walkable (no hopping), steeper ones are walls you slide off or along; a dash into one rides up it (or down it). Shots, the grapple and light all follow the slope, and bots walk up gentle ones. In the map editor, N cycles a box through them and rotate / mirror turn them any way; Quarkology's map editor has Wedge and Corner buttons. Wedges and corners can be grouped with boxes, and the seams between pieces of one group go away, slopes included. Maps with them are format 5 (older maps load unchanged); older game versions can't join servers running this one (protocol 48).
- **Fewer stray outlines**: where a box's edge was only partly against a flush neighbour (a taller step next to a shorter one, a wall meeting a longer wall), the whole edge kept its line; now only the uncovered part does. In hand-made maps, outlines now follow groups: parts of the same group join with no line, even across materials, and separate groups or ungrouped boxes keep theirs. The official maps keep joining same-material boxes.

- **FIX MAP and FIX GAPS in the map editor**: FIX MAP joins same-material boxes that together make one box and removes boxes you can never see (wholly inside solid walls; anything behind glass, water or breakable brick stays). FIX GAPS closes gaps under 1/8 m by stretching the box that's off the grid to the one on it. Each is one undo step.

- **No more holes into the sky behind blown-open brick**: a wall face covered by a thin brick or cobblestone layer was left out of the world, so blowing the brick open showed through to nothing. Those faces are kept now.

- **Cobblestone looks solid**: dark streaks ran out of every corner where three stones met, which looked like gaps in the wall, and each stone was shaded in squares. The joints are now an even width and each stone has one shade.

- **Material picker in the map editor**: clicking a material (for new boxes, or for what's selected) opens a grid of swatches, each drawn in the game's own look and the map's colours. It has three lists: the materials this map already uses, the last 10 you picked (kept between sessions) and all of them. M still cycles. FIX MAP / FIX GAPS now show only when nothing is selected, so the selection's buttons fit on screen.

- **100 new brick, concrete, tile and stone materials** (all of the picks): 30 bricks (colours plus Flemish, English, stack, soldier, herringbone and basket bonds), 20 concretes, 25 tiles and 25 stone walls, each drawn by the game with no textures. - **333 more materials**: your picks from the four earlier rounds of surface looks: 77 general ones (dirt, gravel, slate, basalt, hedge, coral, sci-fi panels and more), 100 nature, 86 industrial and 70 wasteland. Older game versions can't join servers running this one (protocol 49).

# 1.19.1

Everything from the testing builds since 1.19.0: a grapple launcher on everyone's arm and rocket riding, impact sparks and muzzle flashes, explosions that show at once, a tighter head hitbox, two new map materials (NOGRAPPLE and ACID), new and more detailed player and weapon models, an on-screen HUD editor with HUD styles, RENDER SCALE, a built-in BENCHMARK, and more optimized builds of the game with an AVX2 version picked by itself. **The network protocol is now 47 (1.19.0 used 44): 1.19.1 doesn't play with 1.19.0 games or servers**, so update both. Dedicated servers update themselves. Maps saved by 1.19.1 are format 4: 1.19.0 can't open them. Your settings, maps, demos and files are kept.

## Testing builds
- **Testing builds are now numbered `1.19.1.1`, `1.19.1.2` and so on** (tag `test-1.19.1.<N>`): the production version they follow plus a count that starts at 1. The launcher's TESTING channel and the testing servers see them as newer than 1.19.1 and older than the next release, so there's nothing to do as a player. (Between 1.19.0 and 1.19.1 they were `1.19.0.testing.<run>`.)
- **Server owners, once:** a testing server's updater from before this change doesn't know the new numbers and stops the testing server once 1.19.1 is out. Run `sudo sh tools/server/install.sh` once from a checkout of `v1.19.1` (or the `testing` branch), as for 1.19.0 (docs/OPERATIONS.md). It's the last time: from now on servers keep up with every update by themselves.

## Grapple
- **Everyone now wears a grapple launcher on their left arm**, in first person (low on the left, like the gun on the right) and on other players. The rope comes out of its barrel, and the hook's claw flies out to where it latched; while you're hooked your arm lifts toward it. It has its own HUD > GRAPPLE MODEL setting and isn't shown in modes without the grapple.
- **The gun and the grapple launcher now sit further back in the bottom corners** by default, covering less of the screen, and in the same place at every aspect ratio (16:9, 4:3, ultrawide) and FOV.
- **New HUD > GRAPPLE MODEL setting**: move, size, hide and colour the launcher on its own, separately from the WEAPON MODEL.
- **Tilt for both models**: PITCH, YAW and ROLL sliders (-90 to 90 degrees) next to x / y / depth, so each can be placed on all 6 axes. Your shots and the rope leave the moved, tilted barrels.
- **Rocket riding**: the grapple now catches rockets in flight, anyone's, your own too: fire a rocket, hook it and it pulls you along behind it. Only rockets (not knives, syringes, stickies or bolts). The hook lets go when the rocket explodes or after the usual 3 s, range and line of sight limits, you keep your speed and the grapple's cooldown starts. Custom modes can turn it off (GENERAL > ABILITIES > ROCKET RIDE); it's on everywhere else. A new network protocol (47): servers and players need this version.

## Shots and explosions
- **Impact sparks everywhere**: hitscan shots (rifle, sniper, shotgun, laser) now spark where they hit a wall, not only on enemies, and other players' shots spark too. Settings > GAMEPLAY > SHOTS > IMPACT SPARKS turns them off.
- **Muzzle flash** on your gun and everyone else's when they fire. Settings > GAMEPLAY > SHOTS > MUZZLE FLASH turns it off.
- **Your explosions show at once**: your rockets and bolts blow up on your screen the moment they hit a wall or an enemy, and your stickies the moment you detonate, instead of a round trip later. Damage and deaths still come from the server, so nobody looks dead who isn't.
- **Screenshots no longer overwrite each other**: the screenshot key (F12) now saves to a `screenshots` folder in your game data folder, named by date and time, and the notice says the file name. Before, every launch started again at screenshot_0.png and replaced the last session's.
- **Weapon model opacity**: Settings > GAMEPLAY > VIEW > WEAPON MODEL OPACITY makes your first-person gun and grapple launcher see-through (1 = solid, 0 = gone).
- **More detailed weapon models**: every first-person weapon except the locator is rebuilt with more parts (sights, rails, grips, glowing details), up to 20 boxes each. Their size and where they sit on screen are unchanged.
- **New player models**: WIZARD, ZOMBIE and FIGHTER, plus SIMPLE (just the hitbox: a body box and a head box), which replaces SCOUT (anyone who picked SCOUT now gets SIMPLE). STANDARD, HEAVY, ROBOT and KNIGHT and every projectile (rocket, sticky, bolt, knife, syringe, bubble, orb) are rebuilt with more detail. Every model still has the same hitbox.
- **More player models**: PIRATE, NINJA and BANDIT.
- **New map material: NOGRAPPLE** (slate blue with diagonal stripes). It is solid like a normal wall for players, shots and sight, but your grapple hits it and lets go instead of latching on. In the editor it comes after CLIP on the M key and the material list. Maps saved by this version are format 3; older games cannot open maps that use it.
- **New map material: ACID** (glowing toxic green). You wade into it like lava, but instead of killing you at once it takes 10% of your max health when you touch it, then 10% a second while you stay in, so anyone lasts about 9 seconds whatever the mode's health. Your health drops at once on your screen; the death still comes from the server ("dissolved" in the kill feed), and whoever knocked you in gets the kill however long it takes. Regeneration waits while you're in it, and bots walk round it when they can. In the editor it comes after NOGRAPPLE. Maps saved by this version are format 4; this is a new network protocol (45), so servers and players need this version.

The same for every weapon, projectile, the knife and the grapple, crouched or any size. Blasts measure to the body or the head too, and bots aim a little lower so they keep hitting the body. This is a new network protocol (46), so servers and players need this version.
- **Fixed missing box faces**: some faces of stairs and other stacked boxes were invisible in game. # 1.19.0

The first production release since 1.17.0. It collects every testing build from 1.18.0 to 1.18.32: lower input and audio latency, cheaper servers, reworked dashes and the hyper, a gameplay feel pass (taps never lost, enemy movement sounds, a death screen, clearer calls), the new Rubik font and a redesigned menu and settings, and custom modes that can change mode rules, weapons and movement. **The network protocol is now 44 (1.17.0 used 42): 1.19.0 doesn't play with 1.17.0 games or servers**, so update both. Dedicated servers update themselves. Your old demos are converted when the game starts, and your settings, maps and files are kept.

## Movement
- **Two dashes, 0.6 s apart, each recharging in 1.2 s.** From full charges you can use both dashes in the air within about 0.72 s. A spent dash recharges for 1.2 s from the end of the dash that used it, then comes back the usual way: landing refills both, a bunny hop one. On the floor you can dash about every 0.72 s.
- **Holding dash dashes as soon as it can**, and a press up to 0.1 s early is kept until the dash is allowed.
- **Dash aim**: looking straight up, 40% of a dash's speed goes up (was 64%); looking straight down, 90% goes down (was 64%).
- **Hyper (super dash)**: it leaves at 5 m/s faster than you were going (at least 11, at most 36), instead of a flat 30. ## Servers
- **Much less CPU.** A Linux server with players on used about 30% of a CPU core on a small cloud VM. It now uses 10-12%. Each tick also costs 20-30% less: cheaper visibility checks, snapshot packing, bot thinking and lag compensation.

## Bots, rebuilt
- They only know what a player could: a view cone with line of sight, hearing gunfire and footsteps with a rough direction, and memory of where they last saw you. No more 360° vision.
- They react like people (450 / 300 / 200 / 150 ms by level), flick and overshoot, lose track of fast strafers and misjudge leads. Levels are clearly apart; experts are strong but beatable.
- Difficulty no longer depends on the server tick rate. Advanced and expert bots bunny-hop, air-strafe, dash and grapple, and no longer dash into pits.
- **Bots keep off the edges**: they simulate a grapple pull before taking it, never hop or dash toward a drop, and fight away from ledges (falls over every map in testing: 56 -> 5); fewer self-kills with rockets and stickies. They use their real (size-modified) hitbox for objectives, and hide and seek / tag bots no longer pick spots from the previous map. A bot added during a tag match plays the next one.
- Navigation is built in the background at map load (no hitch when the first bot spawns). Fixed bots that sometimes never fired after switching weapons.

## Ranked
- **Your ranked id is proven by your key**, so nobody can play under your id, not even a server you join that passes your connection on to another one: what your game signs names the server you joined. (A dedicated server that players reach at an address it can't see itself, such as a router forwarding a different port or a container, says so with `--own-addr host:port`.) Your ratings, race times and Discord link carry over automatically the first time you start this version (the game keeps asking until the ranking server confirms it, and a match rated before that is merged in rather than replacing your old rating).
- **Match tickets**: a ranked match only counts if the server opened it with the ranking server and the players' results agree. If your game sees a different result than the host's, it reports a dispute instead, and a disputed match is never rated (it's logged).
- **Live ranked matches are locked** (1v1 vanilla, 1v1 laser vampire and FFA instagib; the Viaduct race isn't): no votes, map or mode changes, ranked off, kicks or team switches until it's over.
- **The first player to leave a live ranked match loses it**; the player who stayed can then leave freely.
- **Race times are reported by the server** that saw the run, and impossible splits are refused.
- **Discord links are verified**: run `/link` in Discord, type the code in SETTINGS > DISCORD CODE. Crown roles go only to verified links. Linking shows what becomes public.
- New accounts are provisional for 5 matches (one placement threshold everywhere).
- A reconnect gets its old slot back only if it proves the same ranked id, and an FFA leaver who rejoins is counted once, as the leaver.
- Spectators of a ranked match see health bars, crowns, models and HUD extras again; only the players have them hidden.

## Servers and connections
- **10 s reconnect grace in every game**: your slot, team and score are kept; in a tourney a drop is no longer an instant walkover.
- **Tourneys are seeded** by your average rating across the three ranked ladders (200 if unrated); top seeds get the byes.
- **Hosting shows if your port is reachable**: the pause menu shows the UPnP result and whether friends can actually reach you (green / red with advice), with CHECK AGAIN.
- **Admin is the player hosting the game**, nobody else. `kick` takes a player's name (or id), and `addbot` takes a skill name.
- Joining does a quick address check, so forged packets can't make a server flood someone or kick a player; server-list queries and version-mismatch replies can't be used for amplification; hit rewind is capped by your real ping; chat is filtered and rate-limited; votes check map names and have a cooldown.
- A malicious server or map can no longer write files outside the game folder, crash the game or freeze it; settings from a server that aren't real numbers fall back to defaults. A broken demo, package or server reply fails with an error, never a crash.
- **Hidden information**: your game is no longer sent the health, weapon or firing of players you can't see, nor projectiles out of your sight (wallhacks have less to show). In hide and seek the seeker gets nothing about the hiders during the head start. While you're dead you see what the player you watch sees, and explosions out of sight still sound where they happen. Spectators still see everything.
- **New vote: move a player to spectator** (`callvote spec <name>`, from 3 players): for someone AFK or causing trouble. They stay out of play until the next map. Kicking stays with the host or the server console and can't be voted.
- The ranking server's address is built into the game (only a file signed with the release key can move it); it's hardened against spam, with cached leaderboards.
- **Smoother servers with many players**: line-of-sight checks are spread over the ticks and capped (Midtown with 32 players: worst tick 11-13 ms -> under 1 ms), and sending snapshots allocates no memory.
- Hosted edit sessions no longer hitch every 5 s: the autosave runs off the game thread.
- Stopping or leaving a hosted game no longer freezes the screen for up to 15 s.
- `--own-addr` is explained in the README, and a game hosted from the menu says on the pause screen when players reach it at an address it can't confirm as its own.
- Fixed: a custom mode whose map list started with a blank entry switched the host to a map with no name.
- **Every server box runs a production and a testing server** ("[TESTING]", next port up), each on the latest build of its channel. The testing server only runs while there's a testing build newer than production; otherwise it's off. A load governor shares the machine: when it can't carry both, the empty server slows first, then the one not playing a ranked match, then the other, down to 125 Hz; if that isn't enough the testing server closes until things calm down. Production never closes.
- **Ranked on testing servers and testing builds is played but never rated** ("TESTING SERVER - RANKED NOT RATED"), and the ranking server refuses their results.

- **Your data lives in your user folder** (Windows `%APPDATA%\quark`, Linux `~/.local/share/quark`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/quark`): settings, ranked key, demos, HUDs, your maps. It's copied over on first start, and uninstalling never deletes it.

## Server: less CPU, less bandwidth
- **Snapshot rate:** snapshots are sent at their own rate, separate from the 1000 Hz simulation. The default is 500 per second; `--snaprate N` changes it (1000 = lowest latency, 250 or less = less CPU and upload).
  - Your input is still simulated every millisecond.

  - Result: 172 → 129 bytes per snapshot. With half as many snapshots, upload per player is about 62% lower (≈1.4 → 0.5 Mbit/s).
- **Snapshot buffers** are reused instead of being reallocated every send.
- **An empty server** sleeps between ticks instead of busy-waiting.

# 0.35.0

## Faster frames
- **World culling:** the world is split into 12 m chunks, and only the ones in view are drawn, in a single draw call. Before, every surface was drawn every frame, including everything behind you.
- **World shader:** same image (identical to within 1/255 per pixel), less work per pixel. Map colours are converted once per frame instead of once per pixel, and glow trim and distant scenery skip the lighting entirely.
- **Players, projectiles and effects** outside the view are skipped. Their shadows still show up.
- **F3 stats** no longer sort every frame time twice a second; that could itself cause the spikes it measures.
- **Frame cap:** no longer drifts slightly below the rate you set.
- **Other:** shader uniform lookups are a hash instead of a linear search, and finished sounds leave the audio mixer without shuffling the voice list.

- **SMOOTH EDGES (CHEAP):** one screen-space pass that smooths only high-contrast edges, which in quark means the outlines. Everything else passes through untouched.

# quark 0.19.0

## Netcode
- **Delta snapshots.** The server only sends what changed since the last snapshot your client confirmed receiving. An unchanged player costs 3 bytes and an unchanged mode state 1 byte; mode timers are sent in tenths of a second, so they rarely change. If that snapshot is too old, a full one is sent instead, so packet loss can't break it.
  - With 8 players all moving, snapshots dropped from about 420 to about 180 bytes; when players are standing still they're much smaller still.
  - That's what lets big servers keep higher tick rates.
- **Adaptive interpolation delay.** Other players used to be drawn a fixed 3 snapshots + 10 ms behind (13 ms at 1000 Hz). The client now measures how late snapshots actually arrive (99th percentile) and uses 2 snapshots plus that, between 1 and 50 ms. On a clean connection enemies are drawn several milliseconds closer to where they really are, and the server rewinds less for hit checks.
- **Enemies out of sight aren't sent.** The server checks line of sight 20 times a second. Enemies you can't see arrive without a position, so wallhacks get nothing. Their name and score still reach the scoreboard.
  - Anyone within 20 m (earshot), teammates, and everyone while you're dead or spectating are always sent.
  - A player stays visible for 0.3 s after you lose sight of them, and their movement is extrapolated slightly, so peeks never pop in late.

# quark 0.18.0

## Performance (measured with Tracy, 20 s of a bot match on Harbor)
- **Text draws once per character instead of 9 times.** The 1-pixel black outline is now done in the shader, and UI vertices are half the size (16 bytes). Vertex data uploaded per frame went from about 400 KB to about 85 KB, and 2D drawing from 0.72 ms to 0.15 ms (median).
- **No first-frame hitch.** Every shader and blend state is compiled while the map loads, behind the loading screen, instead of on the first frame of the match. The first in-game frame went from 57 ms to 6 ms, and the worst frame after it from 24 ms to 11 ms.
- **Less shadow work.** Player and projectile shadows are only sampled inside the area those objects can actually shade. Everywhere else, the world and player shaders skip the 4 shadow samples per pixel. This helps most on integrated GPUs and at high resolutions.

## Display and latency
- Display modes: windowed, borderless fullscreen, exclusive fullscreen (legacy).

  - On (default): at most 1 frame queued on the GPU, so your input never waits behind a deep render queue.

Measured with GPU timestamps, so it never stalls the game. Does not include the monitor's own scan-out time.

# quark 0.3.0

## Movement
- Left Shift: dash in the direction you're moving (or forward), 1.2 s cooldown. Keeps your speed if you're already faster.

- Q: momentum grapple (like TF2). Press to fire at what you're aiming at (45 m range), hold to be pulled in. The pull adds to your momentum instead of replacing it, so you can swing. Everyone can see your rope.

## Server tick rate
- The server now starts at 1000 Hz and sends a snapshot every tick.
- During warmup it checks whether it can keep up: late ticks, failed sends, and snapshot loss reported by every player. If not, it steps down to 500, then 250, then 125 Hz (the minimum) and tells everyone.
- quark_server --tickrate N sets the highest rate to try.
- Movement is simulated in fixed 1 ms steps, so it is exactly the same at every tick rate and every frame rate (checked by an automated test: identical positions at 1000/500/250/125 Hz with dashing, bhopping and grappling).
- Other players are drawn 3 snapshots + 10 ms behind: 13 ms at 1000 Hz (was 50 ms).
- Client prediction skips its replay when the server agrees with what was predicted (almost always), so high tick rates cost very little CPU.
- Windows: 1 ms timer precision for accurate ticks; the hosting thread runs at above-normal priority.

# quark 0.2.0

## New weapons
- Sniper (4): 95 damage, hold right mouse to scope in (24 degree zoom, perfectly accurate when scoped, inaccurate from the hip). Mouse sensitivity is scaled while scoped so aiming feels the same.
- Laser (5): continuous beam, 5 damage every 0.05 s (100 damage per second), 32 m range. Other players see your beam.
- Rocket (2): faster rockets (32 m/s), 95 damage direct, splash damage and rocket jumping.
- Weapon slots shown on the HUD. Rifle (1) and knife (3) remain as placeholders.

## Performance and latency
- Netcode: snapshots are now sent every tick (60 per second instead of 30) and other players are shown 50 ms behind instead of 100 ms, halving the visual delay.
- Netcode: the server now runs your input the moment it arrives instead of waiting for its next tick (removes up to 16 ms of input delay). Rate-limited so clients can't move faster than real time.
- Netcode: the shared part of each snapshot is encoded once per tick instead of once per player.
- Engine: maps are now indexed in a spatial grid, so collision, hit detection and line-of-sight checks only test nearby blocks (identical results, about 2x faster on arena, more on bigger maps). Lighting bakes faster too.
- Renderer: shader parameter lookups are cached instead of being looked up by name every frame; no per-frame memory allocation for player interpolation.
- Weapon refire timing stays exact while holding fire.
